summary.headline: BlackBuck FY26 total income rose about 55% to ~715 crore and adjusted EBITDA reached ~190 crore, with first full-year PAT of ~160 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 total income of about 715 crore (up ~55% YoY), adjusted EBITDA of about 190 crore (up ~84%) and PAT of about 160 crore, the first full year of profitability. Q4 FY26 total income grew ~46-52% YoY, adjusted EBITDA was 50.2 crore (up ~30% YoY) and net revenue grew ~31%. Management flagged short-term headwinds from the West Asia conflict on intercity trucking and a temporary suspension of OMC fuel loyalty programmes, while stating long-term retention, ARPU and acquisition are unchanged. Investment in growth businesses (super loads, vehicle finance) continued to weigh on margins, and management declined to give numerical growth guidance.

financial_highlights.change: first full year of PAT profitability
core businesses ~30% YoY in Q4, ~34% for FY
management says it tracks adjusted EBITDA

financial_highlights.metric: Power users (using more than two services)

financial_highlights.value: peaked ~36% in Q1 FY26, stabilised ~31% (per analyst)

segments.name: Core businesses (tolling, fuelling, fuel sensor, vehicle tracking, AIS/GPS)
segments.commentary: Core grew ~30% YoY in Q4 and ~34% for FY26. Tolling GTV grew ~27% YoY, about 90% of payments GTV. AIS device sales doubled QoQ on mandates; basic GPS growing ~15%.

segments.name: Growth businesses (super loads, vehicle finance)
segments.commentary: Growth businesses grew roughly 300% YoY in Q4 per management. Vehicle finance disbursals grew 30% in the prior quarter and a further 25% in Q4; super loads run-rate net revenue is ~15 crore vs ~10-11 crore a few quarters back (per analyst).

guidance_outlook: No numerical growth guidance; management said it has decided not to guide on numbers.
Short-term drag on growth expected from West Asia conflict, mainly on intercity heavy-truck movement; April-May saw drag after inventory moved through March.
Fuel business affected by temporary OMC loyalty programme suspension; some impact absorbed in Q4, some expected in Q1 FY27.
Management expects long-term retention, ARPU and customer acquisition to be unaffected.
Vehicle finance expected to exit investment mode and start generating cash flows by end FY27 (per management).
capex_capacity: Continued investment in growth businesses; teams and product/technology headcount being added in parallel experiments, with AI investment in super loads.
Super loads operating in Bangalore and Hyderabad hubs, plus 10 new cities launched earlier; team scaling continuing in existing cities.
Vehicle finance is asset-light: ~600 crore assets managed by partners, of which ~10% on BlackBuck's own books, used mainly for experiments and co-lending.
demand_pricing: Monthly transacting customers ~8.2 lakh, claimed 25-30% of Indian truckers; 10,000+ offline touchpoints; trucker spends ~45 minutes daily on the platform.
Intercity trucking demand softened in April-May 2026 due to West Asia conflict; revenue largely compounding so impact seen as small but visible.
Telematics: AIS demand driven by mandates in 10 states; basic GPS and cannibalisation by AIS noted.

Management said MLFF is prepaid-based, with 99%+ of payments prepaid per offline information; BlackBuck's revenue is 100% from issuer ecosystem today and it is exploring acquirer-side partnerships in MLFF.
Working capital: over 50% of telematics revenue received in advance; receivables under 3 months; other businesses under 30 days.

qa_highlights.question: Are super load hubs (Bangalore, Hyderabad) at break-even, and are existing cities still being staffed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said unit economics are strengthening as manpower tenures; teams are being scaled rapidly in existing cities as well, and it did not quantify break-even.

qa_highlights.question: Vehicle finance book size and whether BlackBuck has a right to win?
qa_highlights.answer: About 600 crore managed by partners with ~10% on BlackBuck's books; differentiation is digital distribution and data, with 24-48 hour onboarding, but management said the model is not expected to be non-linear as it is a risk business for partners.

qa_highlights.question: Why did profit margins soften and what growth can be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed higher investment in growth businesses; said growth is an outcome of acquisition economics and it will not provide growth guidance.

qa_highlights.question: When will super loads revenue scale from ~5 crore incremental to tens of crores, and cost base rise from ~70-75 to ~100 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management admitted pace could have been faster; said a significant part of the cost increase went to core businesses and vehicle finance, and scale-up timing is one to two years out.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Middle East conflict on revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a drag on growth, not a decline; inventory moved through March but April-May saw some drag on intercity truck activity.

qa_highlights.question: Do growth businesses have contribution-level profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all businesses are contribution-margin positive; negative numbers arise only at EBITDA level or below.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict impact on intercity trucking volumes and trade flows in Q1 FY27.
OMC fuel loyalty programme suspension affecting fuel business revenue.
Margin pressure from growth business investment; adjusted EBITDA margin trended from ~36% in Q1 FY26 to ~31%.
Super loads revenue scale-up pace versus rising cost base; management said timeline is uncertain (one to two years).
Vehicle finance is dependent on partner credit decisions; BlackBuck does not guarantee loan performance.
Senior team departures (three people in SMB/senior team per management) and competitive entry into the space.
summary.management_tone: Confident on core business momentum and long-term strategy, but cautious on the near term, flagging West Asia headwinds and fuel loyalty disruption. Evasive on segment-level profitability, growth guidance and super loads timelines, deferring these to future disclosures.
key_quotes: This is our first full year of profitability at a PAT level.
We generally don't give growth guidance I think this is we've typically helped you guys to plot how to look at the business, how it will scale, etc.
So, the way we look at always is that are there opportunities to pursue.
None of these is a structural change or none of these impacts long-term customer acquisition neither long on customer retention neither ARPUs.

growth.why: Management declined to give numerical growth guidance and no capacity or order backing was quantified; Q4 net revenue grew ~31% and adjusted EBITDA ~30%, with West Asia-related drag on intercity trucking and a temporary OMC fuel loyalty suspension flagged as near-term headwinds into Q1 FY27.
